newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL B BAND CELLULAR BID HINGES ON COURT RULING.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL B BAND CELLULAR BID HINGES ON COURT RULING.

text.p: The awarding of a 15-year cellular concession to a Brazilian-Swedish group cannot be formalized until outstanding legal action regarding the bid has been resolved, officials said Friday.

A Communications Ministry official said Brazil's Superior Justice Tribunal (STJ) must still rule on whether the Tess consortium, which includes Sweden's state-owned Telia, is eligible to take part in the B Band license celloff.
The ministry official said the Sao Paulo state concession could be awarded to another group which came second in the bidding process, should the STJ rule against Tess.
The second-place group was Avantel, made up of Brazilian firms Odebrecht, Camargo Correa and Unibanco bank and U.S-based AirTouch Communications.
The ministry in June disqualified Tess and several other groups from the B Band program for allegedly failing to meet tender requirements.
Tess, like other consortia, won an injunction allowing it to take part in the tender.

The Tess consortium, which also includes Airline Celular and Primave of Brazil, won bidding for the B Band concession area No. 2 covering non-metropoitan Sao Paulo state with an offer of 1.326 billion reais.
The bid was 121 percent above the state-set base price of 600 million reais for the license.
Jose Henrique Castanheira, president of Airline Celular, said he was confident the STJ would rule in Tess' favor.
He said the group had been disqualified for using a translator based in Sweden while ministry rules required translation of bidding documents be done in Brazil.
A decision is expected later this month.
In another legal twist, an official read out a decision by a judge ordering the ministry to keep the sealed bid of another disqualified group, Telet, until the conclusion of its legal case.
Telet had hoped to take part in B Band area No. 2 bidding.
